chapter_title: METHODS OF SEPARATION IN EVERYDAY LIFE

items.title: Handpicking
items.explanation: Handpicking is a method used when two or more substances are mixed, such as small stones and husk from wheat or rice. It involves picking by hand to remove particles based on differences in size, color, and shape. This method is convenient when the particles to be removed are present in small quantities and can easily be picked by hand.

items.title: Threshing
items.explanation: Threshing separates grains from stalks by beating the stalks on a large wooden log. This process removes the heavier components of a mixture, such as bran or air/wind, while leaving behind the lighter grains.

items.title: Winnowing
items.explanation: Winnowing separates grains from husks by blowing them with wind or using air. The process relies on differences in size and density between the components of a mixture.
